cells.tense: Everything is still open right now, and that is exactly how it should be.
cells.ask: Name one shape you noticed today and stop there, not fixing or using it, only letting the name land.
cells.core:
There is nothing you have narrowed down yet, and you are fine with that. You can sit with a situation that is still wet, still moving, and see the shape it is making without needing to hurry it. That is rare, and it is not avoidance. When you stay open about what something could become, what you go on to make is not forced out of a small and tired set of options.

This is what it holds like when it is running well: a pattern and a possibility sit side by side, and neither one has to win today. Keep one small piece unnamed through the day. Nothing needs to close for you to be doing this right, and no one is asking you to prove the openness was worth anything.
cells.sheetLine: You can leave a thing unnamed until it knows its shape.
cells.verb: Nothing is decided yet, in the light before any shape is chosen.
cells.place: A room where each thing arrives as a shape and no particular case follows you in.

cells.tense: You are waiting for the version where every possibility is still real, and it never arrives.
cells.ask: Say one thing out loud that you have already settled, then let it stand even if it feels thin.
cells.core:
A lot is still possible, and you are holding all of it, not letting any one piece land. Every difficult choice stays open a little longer, every answer stays undecided, and the openness has stopped being freedom and started being a place you cannot leave. What you keep from choosing is making you tired, not keeping you free.

The other side is plainer than it sounds. You pick up a piece that is already settled and set it down where you can see it — a small, ordinary act, not a doctrine. One thing already decided, said out, lets the rest start moving again. The next piece will still be there after you pick.

cells.tense: The openness sits behind you now, and you are making from a narrower place.
cells.ask: Pick one small open question today and look only at what is true about it now, not what it became.
cells.core:
The capacity is small and it does not ask for much. Running well, it is one glance at one thing for the shape it is making right now, no verdict and no next step required. That glance arrives unforced. It is the kind of thing you can do in a doorway between two other tasks, and it leaves nothing behind that needs tending.

What you have now is narrower than that. The shapes are still there to see, and you are not standing where you once stood. You do not have to force yourself back into openness. One clear look as a pattern arrives is enough to begin, and that look is available today, in the smallest question you have been holding.

cells.tense: You are choosing a direction in the next moment, and calling it what happens to you.
cells.ask: Before one small next choice, wait three seconds and name the other thing you could do.
cells.core:
Somewhere in the last small choices, one direction was already picked. You did not see it as picking, so the other ways did not show themselves, and it feels like there were no other ways. The pattern that came out of that is real. The sense that you did not make it is not, and it is costing you the sight of your own hand in the room.

With the pen in hand, the next step has a shape you chose, and you can say so plainly without ceremony. That is the whole difference. Openness is not something you earn back. It shows up whenever you let one step be chosen rather than received, and one pause before a small move is enough to feel it.
cells.sheetLine: The next step was yours, and you have been saying it was not.

The sentence that served me was the one about standing where they used to — it implies a known history the map never handed me.
